text: Annamaria Beatrice "Nina" Amenta is an American computer scientist serving as the Tim Bucher Family Professor of Computer Science and chair of the Computer Science Department at the University of California, Davis.[1][2] Her expertise lies in computational geometry and computer graphics, with a notable focus on reconstructing surfaces from scattered data points.[2][3] She was raised in Pittsburgh and earned a bachelor's degree in classical civilization from Yale University, graduating in 1979.[2][4] After working as a computer programmer for over ten years, she returned to graduate school and obtained her Ph.D. in 1994 from the University of California, Berkeley, with a thesis on the relations between Helly's theorem and generalized linear programming, under the supervision of Raimund Seidel.[5] Following postdoctoral research at The Geometry Center and Xerox PARC, she joined the faculty at the University of Texas at Austin and relocated to the University of California, Davis in 2002. She was appointed Bucher Professor and department chair in 2013.[2] Amenta co-chaired the Symposium on Computational Geometry in 2006 alongside Otfried Cheong.[6]
